## functions

namespace functions {

// List of feature categories to compute.

}) => any;

type get_neighbors_sarscov2_vitro = (_: {

// Optional list of feature categories to compute for each neighbor.
feature_names?: string[],
// Number of nearest neighbors to return. Default 5.

// Whether to include task labels for neighbors. Default true.

}) => any;

You are a chemist analyzing drug molecules. Available features for the get_features and get_neighbors tools: molecular_weight, heavy_atom_count, heteroatom_count, logp, tpsa, h_bond_donors, h_bond_acceptors, rotatable_bonds, fraction_csp3, molar_refractivity, complexity, electronic, functional_groups, ring_systems, 3d_properties, structural_alerts, metabolites, pka, ionization, logd, solubility

# Tools

## functions

namespace functions {

// Compute selected molecular features for a given SMILES string. Pass a list of feature names to select which analyses to run.
type get_features = (_: {
// Input molecule as a SMILES string.
smiles: string,
// List of feature categories to compute.
feature_names: string[]
}) => any;

// Find nearest neighbors from the SARSCoV2_3CLPro_Diamond training set with labels, similarity scores, and optionally compute selected molecular features for each neighbor.
type get_neighbors_sarscov2_3cl = (_: {
// Input molecule as a SMILES string.
smiles: string,
// Optional list of feature categories to compute for each neighbor.
feature_names?: string[],
// Number of nearest neighbors to return. Default 5.
num_neighbors?: number,
// Whether to include task labels for neighbors. Default true.
include_labels?: boolean
}) => any;

} // namespace functions<|end|><|start|>user<|message|>Instructions: Answer the following question about drug properties.

One method is to screen a library of small molecule drugs for binding to the SARS-CoV-2 3CL protease using X-ray crystallography.
Question: Given a drug SMILES string, predict whether it
(A) does not bind SARS-CoV-2 3CL protease (B) binds SARS-CoV-2 3CL protease
Drug SMILES: COC(=O)c1c(NC(=O)CCl)sc(C)c1C
Answer:
Please think step by step and use the relevant tools in your analysis. Then put your final choice, (A) or (B), after "Answer:"<|end|><|start|>assistant

# Tools

## functions

namespace functions {

// Compute selected molecular features for a given SMILES string. Pass a list of feature names to select which analyses to run.

// List of feature categories to compute.
feature_names: string[]
}) => any;

// Optional list of feature categories to compute for each neighbor.

include_labels?: boolean
}) => any;

}) => any;

You are a chemist analyzing drug molecules. # Tools

## functions

namespace functions {

// Compute selected molecular features for a given SMILES string. Pass a list of feature names to select which analyses to run.
type get_features = (_: {
// Input molecule as a SMILES string.
smiles: string,
// List of feature categories to compute.
feature_names: string[]
}) => any;

// Find nearest neighbors from the AMES training set with labels, similarity scores, and optionally compute selected molecular features for each neighbor.
type get_neighbors_ames = (_: {
// Input molecule as a SMILES string.
smiles: string,
// Optional list of feature categories to compute for each neighbor.
feature_names?: string[],
// Number of nearest neighbors to return. Default 5.
num_neighbors?: number,
// Whether to include task labels for neighbors. Default true.
include_labels?: boolean
}) => any;

} // namespace functions<|end|><|start|>user<|message|>Instructions: Answer the following question about drug properties.

The Ames test is a short-term bacterial reverse mutation assay detecting a large number of compounds which can induce genetic damage and frameshift mutations.
Question: Given a drug SMILES string, predict whether it
(A) is not mutagenic (B) is mutagenic
Drug SMILES: CO/N=C(\C(=O)NC1C(=O)N2C(C(=O)OCOC(=O)C(C)(C)C)=C(/C=C/c3scnc3C)CSC12)c1csc(N)n1

<|start|>system<|message|>You are ChatGPT, a large language model trained by OpenAI.
Knowledge cutoff: 2024-06
Current date: 2026-04-13

Reasoning: medium

# Valid channels: analysis, commentary, final. Channel must be included for every message.
Calls to these tools must go to the commentary channel: 'functions'.<|end|><|start|>developer<|message|># Instructions

You are a chemist analyzing drug molecules. Available features for the get_features and get_neighbors tools: molecular_weight, heavy_atom_count, heteroatom_count, logp, tpsa, h_bond_donors, h_bond_acceptors, rotatable_bonds, fraction_csp3, molar_refractivity, complexity, electronic, functional_groups, ring_systems, 3d_properties, structural_alerts, metabolites, pka, ionization, logd, solubility

# Tools

## functions

namespace functions {

// Compute selected molecular features for a given SMILES string. Pass a list of feature names to select which analyses to run.
type get_features = (_: {
// Input molecule as a SMILES string.
smiles: string,
// List of feature categories to compute.
feature_names: string[]
}) => any;

// Find nearest neighbors from the SARSCoV2_Vitro_Touret training set with labels, similarity scores, and optionally compute selected molecular features for each neighbor.
type get_neighbors_sarscov2_vitro = (_: {
// Input molecule as a SMILES string.
smiles: string,
// Optional list of feature categories to compute for each neighbor.
feature_names?: string[],
// Number of nearest neighbors to return. Default 5.
num_neighbors?: number,
// Whether to include task labels for neighbors. Default true.
include_labels?: boolean
}) => any;

} // namespace functions<|end|><|start|>user<|message|>Instructions: Answer the following question about drug properties.
Context: SARS-CoV-2 is a coronavirus that causes the COVID-19 disease and has led to millions of deaths worldwide within a few years. Discovering new drugs that can inhibit viral replication would be useful for combatting the virus. One method is to screen a library of small molecule drugs for inhibition in an infected cell-based assay.
Question: Given a drug SMILES string, predict whether it
(A) does not inhibit SARS-CoV-2 replication (B) inhibits SARS-CoV-2 replication
Drug SMILES: CN1C(=O)OC(C)(C)C1=O
Answer:
Please think step by step and use the relevant tools in your analysis. Then put your final choice, (A) or (B), after "Answer:"<|end|><|start|>assistant

include_labels?: boolean
}) => any;

Knowledge cutoff: 2024-06
Current date: 2026-04-13

Reasoning: medium

You are a chemist analyzing drug molecules. Available features for the get_features and get_neighbors tools: molecular_weight, heavy_atom_count, heteroatom_count, logp, tpsa, h_bond_donors, h_bond_acceptors, rotatable_bonds, fraction_csp3, molar_refractivity, complexity, electronic, functional_groups, ring_systems, 3d_properties, structural_alerts, metabolites, pka, ionization, logd, solubility

# Tools

## functions

namespace functions {

// Compute selected molecular features for a given SMILES string. Pass a list of feature names to select which analyses to run.
type get_features = (_: {
// Input molecule as a SMILES string.
smiles: string,
// List of feature categories to compute.
feature_names: string[]
}) => any;

// Find nearest neighbors from the BBB_Martins training set with labels, similarity scores, and optionally compute selected molecular features for each neighbor.
type get_neighbors_bbb = (_: {
// Input molecule as a SMILES string.
smiles: string,
// Optional list of feature categories to compute for each neighbor.
feature_names?: string[],
// Number of nearest neighbors to return. Default 5.
num_neighbors?: number,
// Whether to include task labels for neighbors. Default true.
include_labels?: boolean
}) => any;

} // namespace functions<|end|><|start|>user<|message|>Instructions: Answer the following question about drug properties.
Context: As a membrane separating circulating blood and brain extracellular fluid, the blood-brain barrier (BBB) is the protection layer that blocks most foreign drugs. Thus the ability of a drug to penetrate the barrier to deliver to the site of action forms a crucial challenge in development of drugs for central nervous system.
Question: Given a drug SMILES string, predict whether it
(A) does not cross the BBB (B) crosses the BBB
Drug SMILES: CC(=O)NCC1(c2ccccc2)CCN(CCCC(=O)c2ccc(F)cc2)CC1
Answer:
Please think step by step and use the relevant tools in your analysis. Then put your final choice, (A) or (B), after "Answer:"<|end|><|start|>assistant

}) => any;

## functions

namespace functions {

// Compute selected molecular features for a given SMILES string. Pass a list of feature names to select which analyses to run.

// Input molecule as a SMILES string.

}) => any;

// Find nearest neighbors from the AMES training set with labels, similarity scores, and optionally compute selected molecular features for each neighbor.
type get_neighbors_ames = (_: {

// Whether to include task labels for neighbors. Default true.
include_labels?: boolean
}) => any;

The Ames test is a short-term bacterial reverse mutation assay detecting a large number of compounds which can induce genetic damage and frameshift mutations.

(A) is not mutagenic (B) is mutagenic

Knowledge cutoff: 2024-06
Current date: 2026-04-13

Reasoning: medium

# Valid channels: analysis, commentary, final. Channel must be included for every message.
Calls to these tools must go to the commentary channel: 'functions'.<|end|><|start|>developer<|message|># Instructions

You are a chemist analyzing drug molecules. Available features for the get_features and get_neighbors tools: molecular_weight, heavy_atom_count, heteroatom_count, logp, tpsa, h_bond_donors, h_bond_acceptors, rotatable_bonds, fraction_csp3, molar_refractivity, complexity, electronic, functional_groups, ring_systems, 3d_properties, structural_alerts, metabolites, pka, ionization, logd, solubility

# Tools

## functions

namespace functions {

// Compute selected molecular features for a given SMILES string. Pass a list of feature names to select which analyses to run.
type get_features = (_: {
// Input molecule as a SMILES string.
smiles: string,
// List of feature categories to compute.
feature_names: string[]
}) => any;

// Find nearest neighbors from the AMES training set with labels, similarity scores, and optionally compute selected molecular features for each neighbor.
type get_neighbors_ames = (_: {
// Input molecule as a SMILES string.
smiles: string,
// Optional list of feature categories to compute for each neighbor.
feature_names?: string[],
// Number of nearest neighbors to return. Default 5.
num_neighbors?: number,
// Whether to include task labels for neighbors. Default true.
include_labels?: boolean
}) => any;

} // namespace functions<|end|><|start|>user<|message|>Instructions: Answer the following question about drug properties.
Context: Mutagenicity means the ability of a drug to induce genetic alterations. Drugs that can cause damage to the DNA can result in cell death or other severe adverse effects. Nowadays, the most widely used assay for testing the mutagenicity of compounds is the Ames experiment which was invented by a professor named Ames. The Ames test is a short-term bacterial reverse mutation assay detecting a large number of compounds which can induce genetic damage and frameshift mutations.
Question: Given a drug SMILES string, predict whether it
(A) is not mutagenic (B) is mutagenic
Drug SMILES: C/C=C1/CC(C)C(C)(OC(C)=O)C(=O)OCC2=CCN(C)CCC(OC1=O)C2=O
Answer:
Please think step by step and use the relevant tools in your analysis. Then put your final choice, (A) or (B), after "Answer:"<|end|><|start|>assistant

<|start|>system<|message|>You are ChatGPT, a large language model trained by OpenAI.
Knowledge cutoff: 2024-06
Current date: 2026-04-13

Reasoning: medium

# Valid channels: analysis, commentary, final. Channel must be included for every message.
Calls to these tools must go to the commentary channel: 'functions'.<|end|><|start|>developer<|message|># Instructions

You are a chemist analyzing drug molecules. Available features for the get_features and get_neighbors tools: molecular_weight, heavy_atom_count, heteroatom_count, logp, tpsa, h_bond_donors, h_bond_acceptors, rotatable_bonds, fraction_csp3, molar_refractivity, complexity, electronic, functional_groups, ring_systems, 3d_properties, structural_alerts, metabolites, pka, ionization, logd, solubility

# Tools

## functions

namespace functions {

// Compute selected molecular features for a given SMILES string. Pass a list of feature names to select which analyses to run.
type get_features = (_: {
// Input molecule as a SMILES string.
smiles: string,
// List of feature categories to compute.
feature_names: string[]
}) => any;

// Find nearest neighbors from the AMES training set with labels, similarity scores, and optionally compute selected molecular features for each neighbor.
type get_neighbors_ames = (_: {
// Input molecule as a SMILES string.
smiles: string,
// Optional list of feature categories to compute for each neighbor.
feature_names?: string[],
// Number of nearest neighbors to return. Default 5.
num_neighbors?: number,
// Whether to include task labels for neighbors. Default true.
include_labels?: boolean
}) => any;

} // namespace functions<|end|><|start|>user<|message|>Instructions: Answer the following question about drug properties.

<|start|>system<|message|>You are ChatGPT, a large language model trained by OpenAI.
Knowledge cutoff: 2024-06
Current date: 2026-04-13

Reasoning: medium

# Valid channels: analysis, commentary, final. Channel must be included for every message.
Calls to these tools must go to the commentary channel: 'functions'.<|end|><|start|>developer<|message|># Instructions

You are a chemist analyzing drug molecules. Available features for the get_features and get_neighbors tools: molecular_weight, heavy_atom_count, heteroatom_count, logp, tpsa, h_bond_donors, h_bond_acceptors, rotatable_bonds, fraction_csp3, molar_refractivity, complexity, electronic, functional_groups, ring_systems, 3d_properties, structural_alerts, metabolites, pka, ionization, logd, solubility

# Tools

## functions

namespace functions {

// Compute selected molecular features for a given SMILES string. Pass a list of feature names to select which analyses to run.
type get_features = (_: {
// Input molecule as a SMILES string.
smiles: string,
// List of feature categories to compute.
feature_names: string[]
}) => any;

// Find nearest neighbors from the BBB_Martins training set with labels, similarity scores, and optionally compute selected molecular features for each neighbor.
type get_neighbors_bbb = (_: {
// Input molecule as a SMILES string.
smiles: string,
// Optional list of feature categories to compute for each neighbor.
feature_names?: string[],
// Number of nearest neighbors to return. Default 5.
num_neighbors?: number,
// Whether to include task labels for neighbors. Default true.
include_labels?: boolean
}) => any;

} // namespace functions<|end|><|start|>user<|message|>Instructions: Answer the following question about drug properties.
Context: As a membrane separating circulating blood and brain extracellular fluid, the blood-brain barrier (BBB) is the protection layer that blocks most foreign drugs. Thus the ability of a drug to penetrate the barrier to deliver to the site of action forms a crucial challenge in development of drugs for central nervous system.
Question: Given a drug SMILES string, predict whether it
(A) does not cross the BBB (B) crosses the BBB
Drug SMILES: CO[C@@]1(NC(=O)C(C(=O)O)c2ccc(O)cc2)C(=O)N2C(C(=O)O)=C(CSc3nnnn3C)CO[C@@H]21
Answer:
Please think step by step and use the relevant tools in your analysis. Then put your final choice, (A) or (B), after "Answer:"<|end|><|start|>assistant

<|start|>system<|message|>You are ChatGPT, a large language model trained by OpenAI.
Knowledge cutoff: 2024-06
Current date: 2026-04-13

Reasoning: medium

# Valid channels: analysis, commentary, final. Channel must be included for every message.
Calls to these tools must go to the commentary channel: 'functions'.<|end|><|start|>developer<|message|># Instructions

You are a chemist analyzing drug molecules. Available features for the get_features and get_neighbors tools: molecular_weight, heavy_atom_count, heteroatom_count, logp, tpsa, h_bond_donors, h_bond_acceptors, rotatable_bonds, fraction_csp3, molar_refractivity, complexity, electronic, functional_groups, ring_systems, 3d_properties, structural_alerts, metabolites, pka, ionization, logd, solubility

# Tools

## functions

namespace functions {

// Compute selected molecular features for a given SMILES string. Pass a list of feature names to select which analyses to run.
type get_features = (_: {
// Input molecule as a SMILES string.
smiles: string,
// List of feature categories to compute.
feature_names: string[]
}) => any;

// Find nearest neighbors from the SARSCoV2_3CLPro_Diamond training set with labels, similarity scores, and optionally compute selected molecular features for each neighbor.
type get_neighbors_sarscov2_3cl = (_: {
// Input molecule as a SMILES string.
smiles: string,
// Optional list of feature categories to compute for each neighbor.
feature_names?: string[],
// Number of nearest neighbors to return. Default 5.
num_neighbors?: number,
// Whether to include task labels for neighbors. Default true.
include_labels?: boolean
}) => any;

} // namespace functions<|end|><|start|>user<|message|>Instructions: Answer the following question about drug properties.
Context: SARS-CoV-2 is a coronavirus that causes the COVID-19 disease and has led to millions of deaths worldwide within a few years. Discovering new drugs that can inhibit viral replication would be useful for combatting the virus. One method is to screen a library of small molecule drugs for binding to the SARS-CoV-2 3CL protease using X-ray crystallography.
Question: Given a drug SMILES string, predict whether it
(A) does not bind SARS-CoV-2 3CL protease (B) binds SARS-CoV-2 3CL protease
Drug SMILES: CNC(=O)c1cnc(C)s1
Answer:
Please think step by step and use the relevant tools in your analysis. Then put your final choice, (A) or (B), after "Answer:"<|end|><|start|>assistant

}) => any;

## functions

namespace functions {

// Compute selected molecular features for a given SMILES string. Pass a list of feature names to select which analyses to run.
type get_features = (_: {
// Input molecule as a SMILES string.
smiles: string,
// List of feature categories to compute.
feature_names: string[]
}) => any;

// Find nearest neighbors from the SARSCoV2_Vitro_Touret training set with labels, similarity scores, and optionally compute selected molecular features for each neighbor.
type get_neighbors_sarscov2_vitro = (_: {
// Input molecule as a SMILES string.
smiles: string,
// Optional list of feature categories to compute for each neighbor.
feature_names?: string[],
// Number of nearest neighbors to return. Default 5.
num_neighbors?: number,
// Whether to include task labels for neighbors. Default true.
include_labels?: boolean
}) => any;

<|start|>system<|message|>You are ChatGPT, a large language model trained by OpenAI.
Knowledge cutoff: 2024-06
Current date: 2026-04-13

Reasoning: medium

# Valid channels: analysis, commentary, final. Channel must be included for every message.
Calls to these tools must go to the commentary channel: 'functions'.<|end|><|start|>developer<|message|># Instructions

You are a chemist analyzing drug molecules. Available features for the get_features and get_neighbors tools: molecular_weight, heavy_atom_count, heteroatom_count, logp, tpsa, h_bond_donors, h_bond_acceptors, rotatable_bonds, fraction_csp3, molar_refractivity, complexity, electronic, functional_groups, ring_systems, 3d_properties, structural_alerts, metabolites, pka, ionization, logd, solubility

# Tools

## functions

namespace functions {

// Compute selected molecular features for a given SMILES string. Pass a list of feature names to select which analyses to run.
type get_features = (_: {
// Input molecule as a SMILES string.
smiles: string,
// List of feature categories to compute.
feature_names: string[]
}) => any;

// Find nearest neighbors from the AMES training set with labels, similarity scores, and optionally compute selected molecular features for each neighbor.
type get_neighbors_ames = (_: {
// Input molecule as a SMILES string.
smiles: string,
// Optional list of feature categories to compute for each neighbor.
feature_names?: string[],
// Number of nearest neighbors to return. Default 5.
num_neighbors?: number,
// Whether to include task labels for neighbors. Default true.
include_labels?: boolean
}) => any;

} // namespace functions<|end|><|start|>user<|message|>Instructions: Answer the following question about drug properties.
Context: Mutagenicity means the ability of a drug to induce genetic alterations. Drugs that can cause damage to the DNA can result in cell death or other severe adverse effects. The Ames test is a short-term bacterial reverse mutation assay detecting a large number of compounds which can induce genetic damage and frameshift mutations.

(A) is not mutagenic (B) is mutagenic
Drug SMILES: CN(N=O)C(=O)c1c(N(C)N=O)ncn1C
Answer:
Please think step by step and use the relevant tools in your analysis. Then put your final choice, (A) or (B), after "Answer:"<|end|><|start|>assistant

<|start|>system<|message|>You are ChatGPT, a large language model trained by OpenAI.
Knowledge cutoff: 2024-06
Current date: 2026-04-13

Reasoning: medium

# Valid channels: analysis, commentary, final. Channel must be included for every message.
Calls to these tools must go to the commentary channel: 'functions'.<|end|><|start|>developer<|message|># Instructions

You are a chemist analyzing drug molecules. Available features for the get_features and get_neighbors tools: molecular_weight, heavy_atom_count, heteroatom_count, logp, tpsa, h_bond_donors, h_bond_acceptors, rotatable_bonds, fraction_csp3, molar_refractivity, complexity, electronic, functional_groups, ring_systems, 3d_properties, structural_alerts, metabolites, pka, ionization, logd, solubility

# Tools

## functions

namespace functions {

// Compute selected molecular features for a given SMILES string. Pass a list of feature names to select which analyses to run.
type get_features = (_: {
// Input molecule as a SMILES string.
smiles: string,
// List of feature categories to compute.
feature_names: string[]
}) => any;

// Find nearest neighbors from the AMES training set with labels, similarity scores, and optionally compute selected molecular features for each neighbor.
type get_neighbors_ames = (_: {
// Input molecule as a SMILES string.
smiles: string,
// Optional list of feature categories to compute for each neighbor.
feature_names?: string[],
// Number of nearest neighbors to return. Default 5.
num_neighbors?: number,
// Whether to include task labels for neighbors. Default true.
include_labels?: boolean
}) => any;

<|start|>system<|message|>You are ChatGPT, a large language model trained by OpenAI.
Knowledge cutoff: 2024-06
Current date: 2026-04-13

Reasoning: medium

# Valid channels: analysis, commentary, final. Channel must be included for every message.
Calls to these tools must go to the commentary channel: 'functions'.<|end|><|start|>developer<|message|># Instructions

You are a chemist analyzing drug molecules. Available features for the get_features and get_neighbors tools: molecular_weight, heavy_atom_count, heteroatom_count, logp, tpsa, h_bond_donors, h_bond_acceptors, rotatable_bonds, fraction_csp3, molar_refractivity, complexity, electronic, functional_groups, ring_systems, 3d_properties, structural_alerts, metabolites, pka, ionization, logd, solubility

# Tools

## functions

namespace functions {

// Compute selected molecular features for a given SMILES string. Pass a list of feature names to select which analyses to run.
type get_features = (_: {
// Input molecule as a SMILES string.
smiles: string,
// List of feature categories to compute.
feature_names: string[]
}) => any;

// Find nearest neighbors from the AMES training set with labels, similarity scores, and optionally compute selected molecular features for each neighbor.
type get_neighbors_ames = (_: {
// Input molecule as a SMILES string.
smiles: string,
// Optional list of feature categories to compute for each neighbor.
feature_names?: string[],
// Number of nearest neighbors to return. Default 5.
num_neighbors?: number,
// Whether to include task labels for neighbors. Default true.
include_labels?: boolean
}) => any;

} // namespace functions<|end|><|start|>user<|message|>Instructions: Answer the following question about drug properties.
Context: Mutagenicity means the ability of a drug to induce genetic alterations. Drugs that can cause damage to the DNA can result in cell death or other severe adverse effects. Nowadays, the most widely used assay for testing the mutagenicity of compounds is the Ames experiment which was invented by a professor named Ames. The Ames test is a short-term bacterial reverse mutation assay detecting a large number of compounds which can induce genetic damage and frameshift mutations.
Question: Given a drug SMILES string, predict whether it
(A) is not mutagenic (B) is mutagenic
Drug SMILES: CC1(C)C(=O)N(Cl)C(=O)N1Cl
Answer:
Please think step by step and use the relevant tools in your analysis. Then put your final choice, (A) or (B), after "Answer:"<|end|><|start|>assistant

# Tools

namespace functions {

// Compute selected molecular features for a given SMILES string. Pass a list of feature names to select which analyses to run.
type get_features = (_: {
// Input molecule as a SMILES string.

}) => any;

// Find nearest neighbors from the AMES training set with labels, similarity scores, and optionally compute selected molecular features for each neighbor.
type get_neighbors_ames = (_: {
// Input molecule as a SMILES string.
smiles: string,
// Optional list of feature categories to compute for each neighbor.
feature_names?: string[],
// Number of nearest neighbors to return. Default 5.
num_neighbors?: number,
// Whether to include task labels for neighbors. Default true.
include_labels?: boolean
}) => any;

You are a chemist analyzing drug molecules. Available features for the get_features and get_neighbors tools: molecular_weight, heavy_atom_count, heteroatom_count, logp, tpsa, h_bond_donors, h_bond_acceptors, rotatable_bonds, fraction_csp3, molar_refractivity, complexity, electronic, functional_groups, ring_systems, 3d_properties, structural_alerts, metabolites, pka, ionization, logd, solubility

# Tools

## functions

namespace functions {

// Compute selected molecular features for a given SMILES string. Pass a list of feature names to select which analyses to run.
type get_features = (_: {
// Input molecule as a SMILES string.
smiles: string,
// List of feature categories to compute.

# Tools

## functions

// Compute selected molecular features for a given SMILES string. Pass a list of feature names to select which analyses to run.
type get_features = (_: {

// List of feature categories to compute.

You are a chemist analyzing drug molecules. # Tools

## functions

namespace functions {

// Compute selected molecular features for a given SMILES string. Pass a list of feature names to select which analyses to run.
type get_features = (_: {
// Input molecule as a SMILES string.
smiles: string,
// List of feature categories to compute.
feature_names: string[]
}) => any;
